## Walkthrough

Refactors e2e webhook endpoint readiness into a single-check + retry pattern, parameterizes the webhook Service name, strengthens fake kubectl test assertions to validate the new behavior, and integrates the e2e-common test into the Makefile verify targets.

## Changes

**Webhook Endpoint Readiness Refactoring**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|---|---|
|**Makefile verify integration** <br> `Makefile-verify.mk`|Adds `_e2e_common_test_recipe`, new phony targets `verify-e2e-common-test` (depends on `verify-tree-prereqs`) and `e2e-common-test`, and appends `verify-e2e-common-test` to `verify-checks` so the shared e2e-common test runs during `make verify`.|
|**Webhook endpoint readiness core** <br> `hack/testing/e2e-common.sh`|Exports `KUEUE_WEBHOOK_SERVICE_NAME` (default `kueue-webhook-service`). Adds `e2e_check_deployment_webhook_endpoints_once` to perform a single readiness check comparing deployment desired replicas to ready EndpointSlice endpoints for the service. Refactors `e2e_wait_for_deployment_webhook_endpoints` to call the single-check via `retry.sh` and updates `wait_for_kueue_controller_operator` to use the new waiter with deployment and service name.|
|**Test fake kubectl and assertions** <br> `hack/testing/e2e-common_test.sh`|Updates embedded fake `kubectl` to simulate kueue-controller-manager readiness with differing replica outputs and EndpointSlice polling that returns partial results on first call and full results on second. Strengthens post-run assertions to require exactly two EndpointSlice polling attempts, verify status output appears once, reset fake state/log, wait for the controller operator, and assert EndpointSlice query ordering before dry-run webhook probe.|

  _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_
  
  <details>
  <summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>
  
  🌐 Web query:
  
  `In Kubernetes EndpointSlice, can a single pod backing a Service appear in multiple slices (for example IPv4 and IPv6), and should readiness checks deduplicate by endpoint identity rather than counting IP addresses?`
  
  💡 Result:
  
  Yes. In Kubernetes EndpointSlice, a single Pod can lead to endpoints appearing in multiple EndpointSlice objects when those slices are split by IP family (IPv4 vs IPv6). EndpointSlices are grouped by unique combinations including IP family, and if a Service is available via both IPv4 and IPv6 there will be at least two EndpointSlice objects (one per family) [1][2]. The API also states that for a given Service there may be multiple EndpointSlice objects that must be joined to produce the full set of endpoints [2]. For readiness checks/aggregation, consumers should deduplicate by endpoint identity rather than simply counting IP addresses. The EndpointSlices documentation explicitly warns that endpoints may be duplicated across different EndpointSlice objects and that clients must aggregate and build a complete list of unique network endpoints; it points to kube-proxy’s EndpointSliceCache as the reference implementation for endpoint aggregation and deduplication [1]. Additionally, EndpointSlice’s endpoint readiness fields are per-endpoint (per logical backend) and not something you derive from the number of addresses: `ready` is essentially a shortcut based on `serving` and `terminating` [1][2]. The EndpointSlice API also explains that EndpointSlice objects have an immutable `addressType` (IPv4 or IPv6), so the same Pod’s logical endpoint readiness should be reflected consistently after deduplication across slices of different address types [2].
  
  Citations:
  
  - 1: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/endpoint-slices/
  - 2: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/service-resources/endpoint-slice-v1/

  </details>
  
  **Count distinct ready backend endpoints (dedupe), not raw EndpointSlice IP addresses.**
  
  In `hack/testing/e2e-common.sh` (`e2e_check_deployment_webhook_endpoints_once`, lines 132-138), `ready_endpoint_ips` prints every `.addresses` entry from every `EndpointSlice`, and `ready_endpoint_count` is just `grep -c` on that—so the same ready Pod can be counted multiple times when the Service is split across multiple EndpointSlices (e.g., IPv4 + IPv6), letting readiness pass before enough replicas are actually ready.
  
  <details>
  <summary>🔧 Proposed fix</summary>
  
  ```diff
  -    local ready_endpoint_ips
  -    ready_endpoint_ips=$(kubectl "${kubectl_args[@]}" -n "${ns}" get endpointslices \
  +    local ready_endpoint_ips
  +    ready_endpoint_ips=$(kubectl "${kubectl_args[@]}" -n "${ns}" get endpointslices \
           -l "kubernetes.io/service-name=${service_name}" \
           -o go-template="{{range .items}}{{range .endpoints}}{{if ne .conditions.ready false}}{{range .addresses}}{{println .}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}" 2>/dev/null || true)
  +    local ready_endpoint_keys
  +    ready_endpoint_keys=$(kubectl "${kubectl_args[@]}" -n "${ns}" get endpointslices \
  +        -l "kubernetes.io/service-name=${service_name}" \
  +        -o go-template="{{range .items}}{{range .endpoints}}{{if ne .conditions.ready false}}{{if .targetRef}}{{println .targetRef.uid}}{{else}}{{range .addresses}}{{println .}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}" 2>/dev/null || true)
       local ready_endpoint_count
  -    ready_endpoint_count=$(printf "%s\n" "${ready_endpoint_ips}" | grep -c . || true)
  +    ready_endpoint_count=$(printf "%s\n" "${ready_endpoint_keys}" | awk 'NF' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  ```
